text:
sanjay: heads-up — QA hit a nasty combo in the foreground upload flow on Android 14. when the service loses connectivity mid-upload we sometimes see the token refresh POST duplicated (two identical refresh requests) and occasionally the follow-up user upload stalls for ~20s. repro high on Pixel 8 devices behind corp VPN. anyone seen retry+auth + service shutdown weirdness? :wave:
rina: can you share the client/interceptor stack? ordering often causes these races.
sanjay: default sdk client + our AuthInterceptor does a synchronous refresh (execute()) on 401, and we also have a RetryInterceptor that treats network timeouts as retryable. client built like:
```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor(maxRetries=2))
  .build()
```
paul: that ordering is suspicious — if a connect timeout triggers a retry while AuthInterceptor is doing a blocking refresh you can get duplicated POSTs for the refresh endpoint. also execute() isn't cancellable which bites a foreground service shutdown.
sanjay: exactly. repro steps in sampleapp: start upload in foreground service -> force flaky network -> connect timeout -> SDK retries original upload -> interceptor does refresh (blocking) -> sometimes refresh POST is sent twice. meanwhile the service shutdown path cancels coroutine but the blocking execute() still runs and leaves sockets in CLOSE_WAIT so next request stalls.
rina: two fixes: 1) use a dedicated no-retry client for token refresh calls 2) make refresh call cancellable or use enqueue/await suspend wrapper so service cancellation cancels underlying call. both together should stop duplicates + stalls.
paul: also recommend marking token-exchange endpoints as non-retriable in default RetryPolicy. small config change prevents accidental replay of sensitive non-idempotent POSTs.
sanjay: tried local patch: AuthInterceptor now does:
```kotlin
val refreshClient = client.newBuilder().retryOnConnectionFailure(false).build()
val refreshReq = buildRefreshRequest()
val resp = refreshClient.newCall(refreshReq).execute()
```
and switched execute() -> suspend await with invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }. dup POSTs disappeared and immediate follow-ups didn't stall.
paul: great. add unit/instrumented test: simulate connect timeout + auth-refresh and assert single refresh POST. also test service shutdown cancels in-flight refresh.
rina: small SDK ergonomics idea: add a Builder option `authRefreshClientNoRetry = true` that makes AuthInterceptor use an internal no-retry client by default, and add a Kotlin helper `Call.awaitCancellable()` that registers coroutine cancellation -> call.cancel(). Document both in onboarding.
sanjay: sampleapp patch ready (draft PR) — includes updated AuthInterceptor, sample foreground service changes, and an integration test on Pixel 7/8 emulator. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1755 (draft).
dev-bot: Incident bot: created issue #9022 "duplicate token refresh + stall in foreground service on Android 14" and linked PR 1755 (draft).
paul: one more caveat — when swapping to enqueue/await make sure you use call.clone() if retrying the same request body. also watch for streaming bodies that are not repeatable. add a note in SDK docs about marking endpoints non-repeatable/non-retriable.
rina: agree. add onboarding checklist: interceptor ordering, non-retriable endpoints list, and sample foreground service example showing proper cancellation wiring. small docs blurb will save new devs a lot of pain.
sanjay: i'll add the docs note + sample snippet and run the device matrix. tagging infra to run VPN+Pixel matrix in CI.
ops-bot: infra: scheduled device matrix job (Pixel7, Pixel8) with corp-vpn profile for PR/1755.
dev-bot: CI presubmit started for pr/1755 (draft).
paul: once CI is green, ship as opt-in in next patch and monitor canary. if stable we can make the no-retry refresh client the default.
sanjay: thanks all. will post follow-up when PR lands and when infra runs finish :raised_hands:
